correctness.rationale: The proof integrates \(dN/dt=-N/(c+hN)\) to the unique implicit survivor relation. Equal catches force a common survivor and exactly the necessary-and-sufficient condition \(N_0(1-e^{-T/q})=N_cT/q\). At fixed duration the capture difference is strictly negative for small initial stock and strictly positive for sufficiently large initial stock by the explicit lower bound \(N_i(t)\ge N_0e^{-t/c_i}\), ensuring \(N_i(t)>N_c\); uniqueness of equality plus continuity yields global signs. The function \(B(s)=s/(1-e^{-s})\) is strictly increasing from 1 to infinity, giving exactly one temporal reversal for \(N_0>N_c\) and none for \(N_0\le N_c\). The principal real Lambert \(W\) branch yields its positive time. Reproducible bisection checks 700 parameter quadruples and 1400 strict comparisons; finite tests do not prove real-parameter quantifiers.

originality.rationale: The directly relevant integrated Rogers equation and Lambert-W inversion are acknowledged prior art. Relevant full text of Rosenbaum–Rall 2018 and public records for original 1970s sources were compared at claim/implication level. Their accessible descriptions concern single-predator integrated response, switching among prey types, or coupled population cycles, not the exact threshold for separate fixed-parameter depleted-prey trials. Database and title searches have incomplete coverage; two older primary full texts were inaccessible, and a general scalar-flow theorem could yield a covered qualitative component. These limitations are residual risks, not claims of certified novelty.
residual_risks: Complete texts of Rogers (1972) and Oaten–Murdoch (1975) were inaccessible; publisher abstracts cannot establish full-document absence.
A general deterministic scalar-flow single-crossing result may subsume parts of the classification even if the exact initial-abundance formula was not found.
General international literature searches are not exhaustive; independent originality validation remains outstanding.

value.rationale: Fixed-length closed prey-depletion assays rank two predator search-handling trait combinations by cumulative catches rather than initial instantaneous intake. Opposing attack and handling advantages generate a practical ambiguity not removed by single-agent curves. The theorem provides a sharp experimentally interpretable initial-stock criterion for every trial duration, a unique time reversal and a closed-form switch law. It specifies the exact boundary across a natural two-trait crossing regime, not a one-off numerical sample, arbitrary slice or relabeling of the depletion inversion.
